editorial.headline: Nationally Open, but Blocked for PMA Registration in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Nationally open to 100% foreign ownership, this communications-equipment rental activity is blocked for PMA registration across Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 77396 is the commercial activity of making specialised communications and multimedia equipment available under rental or operational-leasing arrangements without an option to purchase. Its communications side covers radio, television and professional communications machinery and equipment, expressly including walkie-talkies. Its multimedia side reaches the equipment behind creative-content production: image and sound recording tools such as cameras, CCTV cameras, microphones, recording media and lighting, alongside digital-media processing equipment including render farms, motion-capture equipment and three-dimensional scanners. The scope is therefore broad in equipment type but specific in the commercial form: rental or operational leasing.

The register is open to Micro, Small, Medium and Large enterprises. That breadth is important: the activity is not confined in the record to one business scale. The registrant is the business carrying out the rental or operational leasing of this defined range of equipment. A single code can therefore encompass communications gear and the practical tools used for recording, lighting and digital-media processing, provided the activity remains within the stated rental and lease-without-option model.

At national level, the position is open to foreign investment, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, the supplied national record permits full foreign ownership for this activity; it does not set a national ceiling below that level. The cited basis is Presidential Regulations 10/2021 and 49/2021. That national openness is the starting point for a PMA reading, but it is not the conclusion for a business looking to register the activity in Bali.

In Bali, a foreign investor cannot register this activity for PMA today. Bali classifies it as blocked on risk-class grounds: at the Large scale, the OSS risk is Low or Medium-Low across every scope, bringing it within Bali’s moratorium. The provincial rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently; the record dates the cited moratorium trigger to May 13, 2026. The honest result is stark: a national 100% foreign-ownership ceiling does not make this activity registrable for PMA in Bali.
